Evaluate fitted effects on declarative axis grids

Source: R/effects.R
estimate_effect.Rd

Computes selected impulse-response effects and their pointwise uncertainty as joint linear functionals of the fitted coefficients. Axes may vary over numeric values, quantiles, or the fitted domain, or be fixed at a numeric value or a training-data mean or median with an optional standard deviation offset.

Usage

estimate_effect(
  object,
  terms = NULL,
  axes = list(),
  impulses = NULL,
  responses = NULL,
  composition = c("term", "total"),
  grouping = c("population", "deviation", "conditional"),
  groups = NULL,
  reference = list(),
  se = TRUE,
  unconditional = FALSE,
  level = 0.95,
  n = 200L,
  boundary = c("estimate", "bound")
)

Arguments

object

A fitted cdrgam model.

terms

Term labels, or a selector list with optional fields names (term labels), predictors (predictor names, or "*" for any term with predictors), match ("contains", the default, or "exact"), and grouped (logical). NULL selects every impulse-response term.

axes

Named axis requests. Predictor requests are nested under predictors; "*" supplies a fallback for every predictor axis.

impulses, responses

Optional training streams used to recover axis summaries from models fitted before summaries were stored.

composition

Return the selected term alone or add its hierarchy of fitted marginal terms.

grouping

Return population, grouped-deviation, or conditional effects.

groups

Optional grouping levels.

reference

Optional named list of reference values for evaluation axes, using the same request forms as axes. Each request must resolve to one value. A predictor may instead be NA or "default" to leave it at the model default. Names are axis names such as lag or a predictor.

se

Include pointwise standard errors.

unconditional

Include smoothing-parameter uncertainty when supported. Smoothing parameters classified as on the boundary of their range contribute no uncertainty, because the criterion has no local curvature along them. Sparse fits stop with an error when the outer Hessian is not positive definite after those parameters are excluded.

level

Confidence level for lower and upper.

n

Default number of points for fitted-domain grids.

boundary

"estimate" (the default) uses the fitted smoothing parameters. "bound" repeats the calculation with each boundary smoothing parameter set to its profile bound, the largest variance component the data still support, while the other smoothing parameters stay at their estimates. Compare the two to check whether conclusions depend on treating those variance components as zero. "bound" requires a sparse Gaussian REML fit with sparse_control$boundary_sensitivity = TRUE and unconditional = FALSE.

Value

A cdrgam_effect_grid data frame with evaluation axes, estimates, standard errors, and pointwise confidence limits on the linear-predictor scale. Each reference axis adds a <axis>_reference column, which is NA for a model default.

Details

With composition = "total", the selected term is summed with every ungrouped term in its hierarchy: terms on the same by covariate whose predictors are a subset of the selected term's predictors, with the same linear or smooth treatment of each shared predictor. For irf(x, z, k_p = list(NULL, 3)) this adds irf(x), irf(z, k_p = 3), and irf(1) when they are present. A time-invariant term is included below a time-varying term with the same predictors. Under grouping = "conditional", the grouped deviations of those terms at the same level are also added.

reference subtracts the same functional evaluated at reference values of some axes. Axes not named in reference keep their evaluated values. The standard errors account for the covariance of the two evaluations. A predictor whose reference is NA or "default" is left at the model default: every term that involves it contributes zero to the reference. For a centered linear predictor this equals its center. For a smooth predictor it is the training-average contribution implied by the term's identifiability constraint. With every predictor at its default, the reference under composition = "total" reduces to irf(1), the response to an average event.

For example, with composition = "total", x at its mean plus one standard deviation, and reference = list(x = list(at = list(summary = "mean"))), the result is the effect of a one-SD increase in x at each requested value of z. A reference value of z gives differences between the interaction curves.

See also

test_effect() for joint Wald tests of the same functionals.
